reasons: The opinion frames the central question as whether the stop and search were justified under the collective-knowledge doctrine.
The opinion expressly discusses the fellow-officer rule/collective-knowledge doctrine and distinguishes horizontal and vertical collective knowledge.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Specify that the case is key for the vertical-imputation branch of the collective-knowledge/fellow-officer rule.

reasons: The opinion says the DEA task force had probable cause to believe Chavez's vehicle contained narcotics and that the probable cause could be imputed to Patrolman Chavez.
The opinion concludes Patrolman Chavez acted on the strength of the DEA's probable cause when he stopped and searched the truck, and affirmed denial of suppression.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: The holding could be tightened by saying this is vertical collective knowledge and that some communication/order from the officer or team with probable cause is required.
